left.text: One sunny morning, Goldilocks picked flowers at the edge of the wood. A blue butterfly danced past, and she ran after it, further and further from home.

right.text: The butterfly flew away. Goldilocks looked up and saw a little cottage with a green door. She knocked. Nobody answered, so she pushed the door open.

left.text: Inside, three bowls of warm porridge sat on the table. Goldilocks was very hungry. She tasted the biggest bowl. “Ouch! Too hot!”

right.text: She tasted the middle bowl. “Too cold!” Then she tasted the smallest bowl. “Just right!” And she ate it all up, every single spoonful.

left.text: Next to the table stood three chairs. Goldilocks climbed onto the biggest chair, but it was far too tall. The middle chair was too wide and wobbly.

right.text: The smallest chair was just right. She sat down and smiled — then crack! The little chair broke, and Goldilocks tumbled onto the floor.

left.text: Upstairs she found three beds. The biggest bed was too hard. The middle bed was too soft. The smallest bed was just right, warm and cosy.

right.text: Goldilocks pulled up the blanket, closed her eyes, and fell fast asleep. Soon the little bed was full of quiet, sleepy breathing.

left.text: The cottage belonged to three bears. They had gone for a walk to let their porridge cool. When they came home, they stood at the table and stared.

right.text: “Someone has been eating my porridge!” said Papa Bear, in his big deep voice. “Someone has been eating my porridge too,” said Mama Bear.

left.text: Baby Bear looked at his little bowl. “Someone has eaten my porridge all up!” he said in his small voice. Then he saw the chairs.

right.text: “Someone has been sitting in my chair,” said Papa Bear. “And someone has broken my chair!” said Baby Bear, and one big tear rolled down.

left.text: The three bears climbed the stairs, soft and slow. Papa Bear looked at the biggest bed. “Someone has been sleeping in my bed!” he growled.

right.text: Mama Bear looked at the middle bed. Baby Bear looked at his little bed — and there was Goldilocks, fast asleep under his blanket.

left.text: Goldilocks woke up. She saw three bears looking at her, and she was very frightened. She sat up small and still, with her heart going thump, thump, thump.

right.text: “Don't be frightened, little one,” said Mama Bear softly. “We will not hurt you.” Papa Bear nodded. Baby Bear peeped out from behind his mother.

left.text: Goldilocks took a deep breath. “I am sorry,” she said. “I ate your porridge and I broke your little chair. I should have knocked first.”

right.text: “I liked that chair,” said Baby Bear sadly. “Then let's mend it together,” said Goldilocks. “I can hold the pieces while you tap the nails.”

left.text: Papa Bear brought wood and a pot of glue. Goldilocks held the legs, Baby Bear tapped, and Mama Bear tied the seat with string. Tap, tap, click!

right.text: The little chair stood up again, strong as new. Mama Bear cooked more porridge, and everyone sat down to share it — three bears and one new friend.

left.text: When the sun began to set, Goldilocks walked home through the wood. “Next time I will knock and wait,” she said. The three bears waved from the door.

right.text: Mama was waiting with a warm hug. “Did you have an adventure?” she asked. “Yes,” said Goldilocks. “And I made three new friends.”
